title: dark_websites — a reference database of the useful, lesser-known web

facets.obscure: Hidden corners most people never reach — independent search, the small web, the strange-but-real.
facets.niche: Built for one community or craft; narrow audience, high signal.
facets.kitsch: Playful, retro, hand-made, or gloriously useless. The web having fun.
facets.broad: Wide coverage — general reference and gateways that fan out everywhere.
facets.deep: Goes far down — long-form, scholarly, or exhaustive on its subject.
facets.narrow: Does one job and does it well — a single sharp tool or lookup.

sites.name: xeno-canto
sites.description: A collaborative archive of hundreds of thousands of wildlife sound recordings from around the world.

sites.name: tldr pages
sites.description: Community-maintained cheat-sheets for console commands — the practical examples man pages forgot.

sites.name: tilde.town
sites.description: A public unix server and gentle art community — hundreds of hand-made ~user pages on one shared computer.

sites.name: textfiles.com
sites.description: Jason Scott's archive of tens of thousands of BBS-era text files — the writing culture of the pre-web internet.

sites.name: ooh.directory
sites.description: A browsable directory of thousands of personal blogs, sorted by topic and freshness. Blog discovery, solved.

sites.name: oimo.io
sites.description: A collection of exquisitely engineered physics toys and simulations by a single Japanese developer.

sites.name: iNaturalist
sites.description: Photograph any living thing and a community of naturalists (plus a model) identifies it — citizen science at scale.

sites.name: endless.horse
sites.description: An ASCII horse whose legs scroll on forever. That's it. That's the site.

sites.name: earth.nullschool.net
sites.description: A hypnotic live visualization of global wind, ocean currents and weather on a spinnable planet.

sites.name: eBird
sites.description: Cornell's global birding database — live sightings, hotspot maps and migration data from millions of checklists.

sites.name: crontab.guru
sites.description: Paste a cron expression and get it back in plain English. The quick reference for schedule syntax.

sites.name: Zombo.com
sites.description: The infinite promise of the year-2000 web, preserved. You can do anything at Zombo.com.

sites.name: WorldCat
sites.description: Search the catalogs of tens of thousands of libraries worldwide and find which one near you holds the book.

sites.name: Wolfram|Alpha
sites.description: A computational answer engine — ask it math, dates, units, nutrition or physics and get worked results.

sites.name: Windows 93
sites.description: A fully interactive parody operating system in your browser, packed with absurd apps and easter eggs.

sites.name: VirusTotal
sites.description: Scan a file or URL against dozens of antivirus engines at once. First stop for anything suspicious.

sites.name: TinEye
sites.description: Reverse image search that finds where a picture came from and how it's been modified.

sites.name: Tildes
sites.description: A non-profit, ad-free link community engineered for depth of discussion over engagement.

sites.name: The Useless Web
sites.description: One button that teleports you to a random gloriously pointless website. The web's best worst tour guide.

sites.name: SunCalc
sites.description: Sun position, sunrise, shadows and golden hour for any spot on the map, any day of the year.

sites.name: Stellarium Web
sites.description: A planetarium in the browser — the night sky from your location, any time, any date.

sites.name: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sites.description: The gold standard of free scholarly reference — peer-reviewed, constantly updated articles on all of philosophy.

sites.name: Standard Ebooks
sites.description: Public-domain classics re-typeset to modern professional standards, free in every format.

sites.name: Squoosh
sites.description: Drag in an image, compare compression codecs side by side, and shrink it without shipping it to a server.

sites.name: SomaFM
sites.description: Listener-supported, commercial-free internet radio with dozens of hand-curated channels.

sites.name: Smithsonian Open Access
sites.description: Millions of Smithsonian images and 3D models released CC0 — download, remix, reuse, no permission needed.

sites.name: Shadertoy
sites.description: Write and browse GPU shaders live in the browser — some of the most astonishing graphics code on the web.

sites.name: Semantic Scholar
sites.description: AI-assisted academic search from AI2 — citation graphs, TLDRs and influence metrics across 200M+ papers.

sites.name: Search My Site
sites.description: A search engine that only indexes user-submitted personal and independent websites. Zero ads, zero SEO spam.

sites.name: Sandspiel
sites.description: A beautiful falling-sand game — pour water, grow plants, set fires, and share your little worlds.

sites.name: SS64
sites.description: A quietly comprehensive command-line reference covering bash, PowerShell, cmd, macOS and more.

sites.name: SDF Public Access UNIX
sites.description: A free public-access UNIX system running since 1987 — shell accounts, gopher, and a living piece of net history.

sites.name: Rosetta Code
sites.description: The same programming task solved side by side in hundreds of languages. A comparative reference.

sites.name: Radio Garden
sites.description: Spin a globe and drop into any live local radio station on Earth. Wonderfully meditative.

sites.name: Project Euler
sites.description: Hundreds of math problems designed to be solved with programs — each one a small, addictive puzzle.

sites.name: Poolsuite FM
sites.description: An ultra-summer internet radio station wrapped in a Macintosh-flavored 80s interface.

sites.name: Pointer Pointer
sites.description: Wherever you put your cursor, a stranger in a photo is pointing right at it.

sites.name: Poetry Foundation
sites.description: A vast, searchable archive of poems and poets, plus essays and a daily poem.

sites.name: Photopea
sites.description: A full Photoshop-grade image editor that runs entirely in the browser, free, no signup.

sites.name: PhET Simulations
sites.description: The University of Colorado's free interactive science and math simulations, used in classrooms worldwide.

sites.name: Perseus Digital Library
sites.description: Tufts' vast library of Greek and Latin texts with linked translations, dictionaries and grammar tools.

sites.name: Patatap
sites.description: Tap your keyboard and every key paints an animation with a sound. A portable visual-music kit.

sites.name: Orb.farm
sites.description: Sculpt a self-sustaining glass aquarium ecosystem — algae, fish, bacteria — and watch it live.

sites.name: Openverse
sites.description: Search across hundreds of millions of openly-licensed images and audio you can reuse freely.

sites.name: OpenStreetMap
sites.description: The Wikipedia of maps — a free, editable map of the world maintained by millions of contributors.

sites.name: OneLook
sites.description: One search across dozens of dictionaries, with a reverse mode that finds the word from its meaning.

sites.name: Omniglot
sites.description: An encyclopedia of the world's writing systems and languages, lovingly maintained for decades.

sites.name: Old Maps Online
sites.description: Search historical maps from libraries worldwide by place and time. A gateway to cartographic archives.

sites.name: MusicBrainz
sites.description: The open encyclopedia of music metadata — every release, recording and artist, community-maintained.

sites.name: MetaFilter
sites.description: One of the web's oldest link-and-discussion communities, still thoughtful after 25+ years.

sites.name: Lobsters
sites.description: An invite-vetted computing community — like a smaller, calmer, tag-organized Hacker News.

sites.name: LibriVox
sites.description: Volunteers reading public-domain books aloud — thousands of free audiobooks in dozens of languages.

sites.name: Koalas to the Max
sites.description: Divide circles again and again until a hidden picture emerges. Deeply satisfying mouse doodling.

sites.name: Internet Sacred Text Archive
sites.description: A quarter-century-old archive of scripture, mythology and folklore from every tradition, free to read.

sites.name: IndieWeb
sites.description: The wiki and community for owning your own corner of the web — protocols, patterns and pep talks for personal sites.

sites.name: IMSLP / Petrucci Music Library
sites.description: Over half a million scores of public-domain sheet music — practically all of classical music, free.

sites.name: Heavens-Above
sites.description: Precise pass predictions for the ISS and thousands of satellites over your exact location.

sites.name: Have I Been Pwned
sites.description: Check whether your email appears in known data breaches. The canonical breach lookup.

sites.name: GifCities
sites.description: The Internet Archive's search engine for animated GIFs harvested from GeoCities. Under-construction signs forever.

sites.name: Falstad Applets
sites.description: A legendary trove of interactive physics simulations — circuits, waves, fields — hand-built by one person.

sites.name: FRED
sites.description: The St. Louis Fed's free trove of 800,000+ economic time series, all chartable and downloadable.

sites.name: Explorable Explanations
sites.description: A hub of playable essays — learn ideas by fiddling with them instead of reading about them.

sites.name: Excalidraw
sites.description: A virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn-style diagrams. Open a tab, draw, share.

sites.name: Europeana
sites.description: Tens of millions of digitised artworks, books, and recordings from Europe's museums and archives.

sites.name: Dwitter
sites.description: Visual demos written in 140 characters of JavaScript. A whole demoscene inside a tweet's worth of code.

sites.name: Directory of Open Access Journals
sites.description: The curated index of legitimate open-access journals — 20,000+ titles you can read without a paywall.

sites.name: Digital Public Library of America
sites.description: One search box across the digitised collections of America's libraries, archives and museums.

sites.name: Desmos
sites.description: A graphing calculator so fluid it feels like a toy — plot, slide parameters, and share live graphs.

sites.name: David Rumsey Map Collection
sites.description: Over 100,000 historical maps scanned in extraordinary detail, free to explore and overlay on the modern world.

sites.name: Compiler Explorer
sites.description: Type code, instantly see the assembly dozens of compilers produce. Indispensable for understanding what really runs.

sites.name: Chronicling America
sites.description: The Library of Congress's searchable archive of digitized American newspaper pages from 1777 to 1963.

sites.name: Cameron's World
sites.description: A scrolling love letter to GeoCities, collaged from thousands of archived pages. The old web in full glitter.

sites.name: CORE
sites.description: The world's largest aggregator of open-access research papers — hundreds of millions, full-text searchable.

sites.name: Biodiversity Heritage Library
sites.description: Centuries of natural history literature and illustration, scanned and free — where the old drawings of everything live.

sites.name: BetterExplained
sites.description: Math explained intuition-first — why ideas work, not just the formulas that state them.

sites.name: Astronomy Picture of the Day
sites.description: NASA's one-image-a-day tour of the cosmos, running with an astronomer's caption since 1995.

sites.name: Akiyoshi's Illusion Pages
sites.description: Psychology professor Akiyoshi Kitaoka's hand-made gallery of motion illusions that genuinely break your eyes.

sites.name: Are.na
sites.description: A calm, ad-free tool for collecting and connecting ideas, images and links into visual research channels.

sites.name: Open Library
sites.description: An open, editable catalogue aiming for one web page per book ever published, with many free to borrow.

sites.name: Kagi Small Web
sites.description: A live stream of fresh posts from independent blogs and personal sites — the non-algorithmic web.

sites.name: 1MB Club
sites.description: A directory of websites that weigh less than one megabyte — a quiet protest against the bloated web.

sites.name: Wikenigma
sites.description: An encyclopedia of the unknown — a catalogue of gaps in human knowledge and unanswered questions.

sites.name: Freesound
sites.description: A huge collaborative database of Creative Commons sound clips — field recordings, effects, loops.

sites.name: RefSeek
sites.description: An academic search engine for students and researchers, indexing documents, encyclopedias and journals.

sites.name: Neocities
sites.description: Free static web hosting reviving the spirit of GeoCities. Browse a directory of hand-made personal sites.

sites.name: BASE
sites.description: Bielefeld Academic Search Engine — one of the largest indexes of open-access scholarly material on the web.

sites.name: neal.fun
sites.description: A collection of playful interactive toys and visual experiments — 'The Size of Space', 'Deep Sea' and more.

sites.name: The Pudding
sites.description: Visual essays that explain ideas debated in culture through data, animation and interaction.

sites.name: Everything2
sites.description: A pre-Wikipedia collaborative writing community — part encyclopedia, part literary playground, still alive.

sites.name: TV Tropes
sites.description: A vast, hyperlinked wiki cataloguing storytelling devices across every medium. Easy to lose an afternoon.

sites.name: DevDocs
sites.description: Fast, searchable, offline-capable API documentation for hundreds of languages and libraries in one place.

sites.name: Can I use
sites.description: Browser support tables for HTML, CSS and JS features. The reference for what's safe to ship.

sites.name: regex101
sites.description: Build and debug regular expressions with live highlighting and a plain-English explanation of each token.

sites.name: explainshell
sites.description: Paste a shell command and it annotates every flag and argument with the matching man-page text.

sites.name: CyberChef
sites.description: The 'cyber swiss-army knife' — encode, decode, encrypt, parse and analyze data by stacking operations.

sites.name: Shapecatcher
sites.description: Draw a symbol with your mouse and it finds the matching Unicode character.

sites.name: Forvo
sites.description: Hear how words and names are pronounced by native speakers in dozens of languages.

sites.name: Detexify
sites.description: Draw a math symbol and get the LaTeX command for it. A lifesaver while writing papers.

sites.name: Wikidata
sites.description: The structured, machine-readable knowledge base behind Wikipedia. Query it with SPARQL.

sites.name: Our World in Data
sites.description: Research and interactive charts on global living conditions — health, energy, poverty, climate.

sites.name: Online Etymology Dictionary
sites.description: Where words come from — origins, first known use, and how meanings drifted over centuries.

sites.name: The Public Domain Review
sites.description: Essays and collections drawn from out-of-copyright art, books and film. Beautiful historical oddities.

sites.name: Low-Tech Magazine (solar)
sites.description: A solar-powered website about sustainable, low-energy tech. Goes offline when the sun doesn't shine.

sites.name: Atlas Obscura
sites.description: A crowd-sourced catalogue of the world's wonders, curiosities and hidden places.

sites.name: Gwern.net
sites.description: Exhaustive long-form essays on psychology, statistics, AI and the obscure — heavily cited and endlessly deep.

sites.name: Connected Papers
sites.description: Enter one paper and get a visual graph of the works around it. A map for a literature review.

sites.name: Bartosz Ciechanowski
sites.description: Interactive explainers of how things work — GPS, gears, light, sound — with hand-built simulations you can drag.

sites.name: arXiv
sites.description: Open-access preprints across physics, math, CS, biology and more — research before it hits a journal.

sites.name: The Library of Babel
sites.description: Every possible page of text that could ever be written, generated on demand. A Borges story made browsable.

sites.name: OEIS — Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences
sites.description: Paste in a number sequence and find out what it is. 370,000+ sequences with references and code.

sites.name: Wiby
sites.description: A search engine that surfaces classic, simple personal websites. Hit 'surprise me' for a random one.

sites.name: Wayback Machine
sites.description: See any page as it looked on a given date. Indispensable for dead links and vanished sources.

sites.name: Project Gutenberg
sites.description: 70,000+ free ebooks whose copyright has expired in the US. The original digital library.

sites.name: Marginalia Search
sites.description: An independent search engine that favors text-heavy, non-commercial pages — the old web you can't find on Google.

sites.name: Internet Archive
sites.description: Books, music, software, films and the Wayback Machine. A non-profit library of millions of free items.
